drivingQuestion: How can the mishna call Miriam's seven-day reward for one hour 'measure for measure'?
outcomeNote: Abaye's emendation is challenged by Rava in the next unit

segments.he: וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן הַטּוֹבָה מִרְיָם וְכוּ׳. מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם — חֲדָא שַׁעְתָּא, הָכָא — שִׁבְעָה יוֹמֵי! אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אֵימָא: וּלְעִנְיַן הַטּוֹבָה אֵינוֹ כֵּן.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «And the same» is so «with regard to the» reward for «good» deeds. «Miriam» waited for the baby Moses for one hour at the shore of the Nile; therefore, the Jewish people delayed their travels in the desert for seven days to wait for her when she was smitten with leprosy. The Gemara asks: «Are» these matters «comparable? There,» Miriam waited «one hour,» while «here,» the Jewish people waited for her for «seven days. Abaye said: Say» this with a slight change: «And with regard to» the repaying of «good it is not so,» as a person is not rewarded precisely measure for measure, as the reward may be greater than the good deed.
